2607.13103.title: Disentangling Knowledge States with Ability and Proficiency Modeling for Knowledge Tracing
2607.13103.paper_summary: Knowledge tracing (KT) aims to predict students' future performance by modeling their evolving knowledge states from historical interactions. Existing KT methods usually treat the raw interaction sequence as a unified behavioral process, overlooking the phase-specific nature of learning behaviors. Our preliminary observations show that students are more likely to correctly answer previously failed knowledge concepts after sufficient practice, suggesting a transition from ability-building to proficiency-oriented learning. Motivated by this, we propose Phase-Aware Knowledge Tracing (PAKT), a KT framework that decomposes student interactions into ability and proficiency phases based on the tailored decomposition mechanism. To effectively exploit the decomposed sequences, we design a multi-branch Transformer with a type-aware readout module to jointly capture phase-specific and holistic knowledge states. We further provide a causal analysis to reveal the confounding bias caused by entangling complex learning behaviors in phase-agnostic KT models. Extensive experiments on six public benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms representative baselines, with a maximum AUC gain of 1.33% and an average gain of 0.82%.
2607.13103.paper_summary_zh: 知識追蹤（KT）旨在通過建模學生從歷史互動中演變的知識狀態來預測學生的未來表現。現有的KT方法通常將原始互動序列視為統一的行為過程，忽略了學習行為的階段特性。我們的初步觀察顯示，學生在經過充分練習後，更有可能正確回答之前失敗的知識概念，這表明從能力建設轉向以熟練度為導向的學習。受到此啟發，我們提出了階段感知知識追蹤（PAKT），這是一個KT框架，根據量身定制的分解機制將學生互動分解為能力和熟練度階段。為了有效利用分解後的序列，我們設計了一個多分支的Transformer，並配備了一個類型感知的讀出模塊，以共同捕捉階段特定和整體的知識狀態。我們進一步提供了一個因果分析，以揭示在無階段KT模型中因纏結複雜學習行為而產生的混淆偏差。在六個公共基準上的廣泛實驗表明，我們的方法始終優於代表性基準，最大AUC增益為1.33%，平均增益為0.82%。
